articleTitle: Variable Frequency Oscillator-Based Resistive Sensor Interfaces Using VCII
publicationTitle: 2024 International Workshop on Quantum & Biomedical Applications, Technologies, and Sensors (Q-BATS)
abstract: This work deals with the realization of oscillator-based resistive sensor interfaces using a second-generation voltage conveyor (VCII). In particular, novel configurations of sinusoidal variable frequency oscillators (VFO) are presented and analyzed in detail. As discussed, the oscillation frequency can be tuned by varying a single resistor in the circuit. To the authors’ best knowledge, this is the first reported case of sinusoidal single-resistor controlled oscillators (SRCO) using VCII. Thanks to this property, the circuit is a very ideal candidate for implementing an electronic interface for resistive sensors. A theoretical analysis of the circuits is conducted to discuss their operation and outline the design process. Finally, simulated and experimental results using commercially available components are presented to validate the theoretical analysis and assess the circuit performance as resistive sensor interfaces.

articleTitle: Analyzing Password Security in Wi-Fi Networks Using The Airgeddon Script
publicationTitle: 2024 International Workshop on Quantum & Biomedical Applications, Technologies, and Sensors (Q-BATS)
abstract: Wi-Fi is a wireless network technology that allows computers, smartphones, tablets, consoles, etc. to connect and communicate with each other via radio waves. Today, Wi-Fi networks have become an integral part of our interconnected world, providing ubiquitous connectivity and convenience. One of the main problems of Wi-Fi networks is password security. In this paper we will analyze the security of passwords in Wi-Fi networks, using the Airgeddon tool and applying brute force and dictionary attacks. By capturing handshakes on different Wi-Fi networks, we estimate the time needed to decrypt them, while simultaneously analyzing the hardware performance as well as the effectiveness of brute force and dictionary attacks. The findings suggest that adoption of strong password practices, including complex combinations of characters, avoiding common phrases or acronyms, using long and varied passwords as well as avoiding frequent repetitions, improve the security of Wi-Fi networks.

articleTitle: Quantum-Enhanced Blockchain for Maritime Cybersecurity: Leveraging Advanced Random Number Generation to Secure Maritime Operations
publicationTitle: 2024 International Workshop on Quantum & Biomedical Applications, Technologies, and Sensors (Q-BATS)
abstract: The maritime services sector is increasingly digitized to improve operational efficiency, safety, and sustainability. However, this digital transformation also exposes the industry to significant cybersecurity risks, such as data breaches, hacking, and disruptions to navigation systems. Addressing these vulnerabilities is crucial to maintaining the integrity and safety of maritime operations. This paper explores the application of quantum random generation for quantum blockchain technology, enhanced with advanced quantum random number generation, as a robust solution to these cybersecurity challenges. By utilizing the Barkhausen effect for generating high-quality random numbers [2][6], and integrating Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) [4], this approach provides a fortified defense against cyber threats, including those posed by future quantum computing technologies.

articleTitle: A Novel AC Wheatstone Bridge-Based Analog Interface for RC Biosensor Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Workshop on Quantum & Biomedical Applications, Technologies, and Sensors (Q-BATS)
abstract: In this paper, a novel electronic interface circuit for RC biosensor applications is proposed and analyzed. The circuit is based on the self-balancing Wheatstone bridge, which allows for a larger dynamic range with respect to traditional bridge methods. Differently from similar previously proposed solutions that operate with purely resistive or capacitive sensors, the circuit is meant to be used with a biosensor that has a more elaborated RC equivalent circuit. In particular, it is shown that, under certain conditions discussed in the text, the system is able to measure the resistance value of the equivalent circuit of this sensor. The operation of the circuit is described in detail, as well as the results and measurements performed on a practical discrete-component implementation of the circuit.

articleTitle: Preliminary analysis on the use of Tiny Machine Learning for the exploitation of biosensors in emotional state estimation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Workshop on Quantum & Biomedical Applications, Technologies, and Sensors (Q-BATS)
abstract: Automatic emotion recognition involves various fields that use human emotional reactions. This contribution exploits the use of low-cost sensors, among the various methods implemented or researched that make use of cameras or expensive medical instrumentation. The provided setup employs contacting and skin-penetrating methods and electrodes for detecting human emotions and measuring their intensity. The results of the analysis proposed can be adapted to different kind of emotions, measuring their intensity of the signal’s feedback and proposing their classification.The proposed approach that classifies emotions through sensor measurements is presented to preliminarily assess application areas and potential results. This work aims to be a model for researchers using assessment and analysis of human emotions, when it is necessary to choose an appropriate method that makes use of low-cost, off-the-shelve electronic sensors.

articleTitle: A Quantum-Cascade Laser based Cantilever-Enhanced photoacoustic sensor for simultaneous N2O and CO detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Workshop on Quantum & Biomedical Applications, Technologies, and Sensors (Q-BATS)
abstract: This work aims to develop a photoacoustic-based trace-gas sensor exploiting the sensitivity enhancement provided by a silicon-based cantilever as the acoustic-to-voltage transducer and by its coupling with a custom-made acoustic resonator and a medium-finesse Fabry-Pérot optical cavity. Thanks to the exploitation of a tunable continuous-wave mid-infrared Quantum Cascade Laser, our sensor can simultaneously address N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O and CO roto-vibrational transitions with a detection sensitivity at the part-per-billion level.

articleTitle: Detection of Fatty Acids in Tomato Seeds Oil Through a Zeolite-PID System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Workshop on Quantum & Biomedical Applications, Technologies, and Sensors (Q-BATS)
abstract: Seed oils are vegetable oils extracted from the seeds of various plants. These oils can be obtained from waste processing, such as fruit and vegetable seeds, which would otherwise be discarded thus helping to reduce waste and enhances the value of food industry by-products. Tomato seeds oil (TSO) is characterized by high concentration of volatile organic compounds (VOCs), which includes fatty acids, vitamins, antioxidants and other compounds resulting in beneficial effect on human health. VOCs levels can be used as fingerprint of the TSO. Hereafter, a VOC sensor for the analysis of tomato seeds oil was developed. The VOCs analysis allows quality assessment through the monitoring of specific fatty acids contained in the sample. A sensor based on photoionization (PID) coupled with a thin zeolite layer was used for the adsorption/desorption of specific molecules trapped within the porous framework. The latter was obtained by thermal desorption analysis. Results evidenced the sensor capability to detect and discriminate between oleic acid and other VOCs inside the oil samples, even at low concentration, based on their dimension and ionization energy.

articleTitle: Gait Parameters Evaluation with Elastomer Based Time-Frequency Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Workshop on Quantum & Biomedical Applications, Technologies, and Sensors (Q-BATS)
abstract: This paper proposes a time-frequency analysis based on Short Time Fourier Transform to extract gait parameters from a strain sensor attached to the knee. Five healthy subjects participated in the study, performing walking, jogging and running on a motorized treadmill according to their habits. The treadmill speed ranged from a minimum of 1.5 km/h to a maximum of 14 km/h. The sensor is a fully stretchable and lightweight capacitor, based on a elastomer, allowing for easy integration into clothing. From the voltage measured at the sensor output, the stride frequency was estimated using the proposed method, and its relationship with speed was determined. From these parameters, the stride length was then extracted and modeled. The results demonstrate the feasibility of applying a time-frequency analysis to estimate fundamental spatiotemporal gait parameters, using a single elastomeric sensor. This suggests its potential application in sports and for individuals with motor neuron diseases.

articleTitle: A comparative study on analyzing the terminal performance indicators – Durres container terminal case
publicationTitle: 2024 International Workshop on Quantum & Biomedical Applications, Technologies, and Sensors (Q-BATS)
abstract: Durres Port is Albania's biggest commercial port. The port has significantly increased cargo handling volume over the last two decades. In 2022, the overall volume of seaborne cargoes in Albania peaked at 6 248 000 tons, of which 5 975 432 tons (combined with new capacities at Romano Port- tons), or 95,6%, were handled at Durres Port. The container terminal handled about 1753126 tons or 39,5% of the port's total volume. Terminal limitation appeals for improved performance indicators such as the ship waiting Time at arrival, terminal idle Time, daily handling rate, etc. This paper analyzes the main indicators of container terminals and identifies the potential for facing future traffic challenges. Methodology: Performance indicators will be analyzed through statistics, paired t-tests will be calculated, and multiple linear regression will be run. T-test and multiple linear regression revealed that the overall Time a ship spends in port is significantly affected by ship size, ship waiting Time at the pilot station, and idle Time at berth. The indicators are based on the World Bank Container Port Performance Index Report. Conclusion: The research offers a clear understanding of the key indicators that need to be improved to face the increasing traffic volume of the terminal.

articleTitle: Analysis of Antioxidant Power and Application of Cherry Tomato Seeds
publicationTitle: 2024 International Workshop on Quantum & Biomedical Applications, Technologies, and Sensors (Q-BATS)
abstract: Tomato seeds are one of by-products of industrial processing of tomatoes, mostly treated as biowaste. Due to their chemical composition that includes carotenoids, polyphenols, dietary fibers, fatty acids, proteins, amino acids and other components, their beneficial effect on human health has been recently recognized. In this research, the antioxidant power (AP) of cherry tomato seeds was measured as a function of storage conditions. Electron spin resonance (ESR) coupled with 2,2-diphenyl-1-picrylhydrazyl (DPPH) radical, used as a scavenging object, was applied to investigate the ethanolic extracts of seeds. Results have shown that the storage conditions have an important role on AP. It was found that freezing for 24 hours has a favorable effect on AP because of its favorable effect on the amount of lycopene and ascorbic acid. Moreover, seeds stored in the refrigerator (4 °C) and frozen (−18 °C) show higher antioxidant power than the same seeds stored at room temperature.

articleTitle: Smart Chair Based On Fiber Bragg Grating Technology for Cardiorespiratory Monitoring in Video Terminal Workers
publicationTitle: 2024 International Workshop on Quantum & Biomedical Applications, Technologies, and Sensors (Q-BATS)
abstract: Technological developments over the past few decades have drastically changed work environments, prioritizing cognitive over physical activity, thus resulting in an increase of video terminal workers. Monitoring the psychophysical status of workers may be performed by physiological indicators like respiratory (RR) and heart rate (HR), as their alteration frequently refer to worker’s stress conditions. Nearable technologies like instrumented chairs and cushions are gaining momentum in this scenario due to their unobtrusive nature enabling long-term monitoring without compromising user comfort and mobility. Among sensing solutions employed in the framework of physiological monitoring, fiber Bragg grating sensors (FBGs) are emerging as promising one due to their several advantages over electrical sensors. This study reports a smart chair equipped with a circular, flexible FBG-based sensing element in its backrest conceived for cardiorespiratory monitoring of video terminal workers. The performance of the proposed system in the estimation of RR and HR were assessed in five healthy volunteers under both physiological and pathological breathing conditions (i.e., quiet breathing and tachypnea). Results demonstrate the potential of this nearable device for HR and RR monitoring in occupational settings.

articleTitle: Design of a Voltage-Conveyor Based Read-out Circuit for ECG Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 International Workshop on Quantum & Biomedical Applications, Technologies, and Sensors (Q-BATS)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a VCII-based read-out circuit and for ECG monitoring employing second generation voltage conveyors (VCIIs) as active blocks. Starting from a quick overview of VCII, the paper describes the whole interface, composed by three active blocks and one passive filter, and its operation. The proposed circuit was simulated by LT-SPICE simulator firstly designing the internal blocks at transistor level, in 0.35 μm standard CMOS technology, and then using the commercially available device AD844 to demonstrate the validity of the designed circuit also with experimental measurements. The voltage gain is tunable by changing some resistance values in the different stages of the amplifier. In the proposed solution, the differential voltage gain has been set to more than 60 dB, while the common mode gain is about -15 dB. Aim of this research is to test the performance of biological signal amplifiers using the current-mode approach (in particular, VCII) which is still underutilized in this context. The goal is to provide a more efficient and versatile system for biomedical applications.

articleTitle: Heart rate monitoring and cardiovascular stiffness estimation with Fiber Bragg Grating sensors embedded in soft patches
publicationTitle: 2024 International Workshop on Quantum & Biomedical Applications, Technologies, and Sensors (Q-BATS)
abstract: The impact that cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) have on the population puts the scientific community in a state of strong concern. CVDs represent, in fact, the main cause of deaths in the adult population worldwide. Among the main cardiovascular diseases, we find ischemic cardiomyopathy, ischemic stroke, myocardial infarction and peripheral vascular pathologies. The increase in deaths caused by cardiovascular diseases is constantly increasing, thus demanding for improved early diagnosis that can both limit the number of deaths per year and reduce the economic engagement related to the healthcare. In this context, here, to support timely diagnosis, we propose a minimally invasive sensor, based on Fiber Bragg Grating (FBG), embedded in a soft silicone patch to increase its pressure sensitivity. The proposed sensor is able to monitor the heart rate, and, from the second derivative of the processed signal, it is possible to get important information about cardiovascular stiffness.

articleTitle: Interplay of Textiles and Gold Nanoparticles for NH3 Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Workshop on Quantum & Biomedical Applications, Technologies, and Sensors (Q-BATS)
abstract: Ammonia detection is of particular interest in breath monitoring due to its diagnostic potential, being linked to several gastric, hepatic, renal, and pulmonary diseases. However, breath samples are particularly complex and extracting the required information is a challenge. Standard equipment and existing sampling methods contain several drawbacks that need to be overcome. Here, we investigate a novel room-temperature gas sensor technology based on the use of cotton and gold nanoparticles as an alternative, simple, and inexpensive tool for ammonia detection. Fabrication and characterization steps of the textile sensor are described in detail. The preliminary results of our feasibility study show fast and repeatable sensor response when the sensor is exposed to 23% ammonia in a background of dry nitrogen.

articleTitle: Characterization of the Performance of Hydrogenated Amorphous Silicon Junction Field-Effect Transistors as Sensor Preamplifier
publicationTitle: 2024 International Workshop on Quantum & Biomedical Applications, Technologies, and Sensors (Q-BATS)
abstract: This study focuses on an extensive investigation of the performance of hydrogenated amorphous silicon (a-Si:H) junction field-effect transistors (JFETs) as sensor preamplifier for Lab-on-Chip (LoC) applications. The integration of a-Si:H JFETs into LoC systems provides a compact and efficient solution for analog signal preamplification, crucial for accurate sensor data processing. By systematically varying the intrinsic and n-type layer thicknesses, we fabricated and characterized multiple JFET devices, and analyzed their electrical behavior through extensive measurements. The measured characteristics allowed us to determine the optimal deposition parameters to be used to achieve the best transconductance values. The results underscore the potential of a-Si:H technology in creating more integrated, efficient, and portable diagnostic tools for biomedical and other analytical fields.

articleTitle: Opportunities and Challenges in Monitoring the Effects of Thermal Treatments for Cancer Removal by Fiber Bragg Grating Sensors
publicationTitle: 2024 International Workshop on Quantum & Biomedical Applications, Technologies, and Sensors (Q-BATS)
abstract: Minimally invasive hyperthermal treatments (HTTs) are clinically accepted for treating many localized tumors (e.g., pancreas, lung, liver, kidney, prostate, and thyroid). An open need in these treatments is to avoid both under and over-treatment to destroy the tumor while sparing the surrounding healthy structures. Many physical parameters of the biological tissue can be useful in adjusting the treatment settings adequately and answering the mentioned need. Indeed, the temperature dependance of many physiological parameters contains a wealth of crucial information to understand the tissue status and optimize the thermal dose. Recently, advances in many sensing solutions based on different working principles and to monitor various physical parameters are gaining interest to provide quantitative feedback that may effectively help surgeons in minimally invasive thermal treatments for localized tumors. This article focuses on one of the most popular measuring techniques (fiber Bragg grating sensors, FBGs) used in this field mainly to measure tissue temperature. Indeed, tissue damage is related to both temperature and exposure time. We described the sensing mechanism of FBGs, their main features, the advantages and risks of using these sensors in minimally invasive thermal treatments, and how to optimize the design of measuring systems based on FBGs to monitor the effects of thermal treatments. Finally, we discuss our experience and other significant studies concerning the application of FBGs in this area, highlighting their role in advancing HTTs.

articleTitle: An AI-IoT Based Non-Invasive Solution for Predicting Glucose Levels
publicationTitle: 2024 International Workshop on Quantum & Biomedical Applications, Technologies, and Sensors (Q-BATS)
abstract: Diabetes mellitus is a global health concern with rising complications from poorly managed blood glucose levels. Traditional blood sugar monitoring methods rely on invasive techniques requiring finger pricking, which can be inconvenient and discourage frequent checks. Nevertheless, noninvasive blood glucose monitoring offers a promising alternative, potentially improving patient compliance and diabetes management. This study aims to develop a non-invasive solution for measuring blood glucose levels using the internet of things (IoT): photo-plethysmography (PPG) and galvanic skin response (GSR) sensors together, with Artificial Intelligence (AI), specifically Long Short-Term Memory model (LSTM). To ensure a comprehensive evaluation, data was collected from two sources: 20 participants diagnosed with diabetes at Hakim Saadan Hospital<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup> in Biskra, Algeria, and an additional 30 healthy subjects recruited from Biskra University in Algeria. The proposed system includes a comfortable wearable device and a Django web application for data visualization and management.

articleTitle: Evaluation and monitoring of SAR and temperature during an indoor Wi-Fi call
publicationTitle: 2024 International Workshop on Quantum & Biomedical Applications, Technologies, and Sensors (Q-BATS)
abstract: The increased use of wireless local area networks (WI-FI) has led to potential daily overexposure to radio-frequency electromagnetic fields in both the home and work environment. The aim is to provide an assessment of the biological effects on the human body of electromagnetic fields in the Wi-Fi range under different exposure conditions, based on studies conducted so far. The work presents the acquisition and monitoring system through the realisation of an electronic device capable of processing the signal from sensors appropriately positioned within an environment. The results produced provided effective answers for the evaluation of temperature distribution on the surface of the human body due to the incidence of electromagnetic fields. The device acquires data from the sensors and detects temperature and SAR values when the user is positioned on the axis of maximum directivity of the directional antennas.

articleTitle: Testing Intelligent Traffic Control Solutions efficiency in reducing traffic and pollution in Tirana*
publicationTitle: 2024 International Workshop on Quantum & Biomedical Applications, Technologies, and Sensors (Q-BATS)
abstract: Urban traffic congestion is an issue that metropolitan regions face throughout the world. It has a substantial negative influence on the levels of pollution in the environment and lowers the standard of living in urban areas. This study examines the efficacy of three different traffic control methods in the urban environment of Tirana, Albania: conventional static, actuated, and delay-based. The study assesses how effective they are in controlling traffic flow and reducing emissions by using simulation approaches. Using the Simulation of Urban Mobility (SUMO) tool, the investigation compares the performance of these systems, focusing on key indicators such as time spent in traffic, fuel consumption, and emission levels. Contrary to initial assumptions, the simulations reveal the actuated system as the most efficient, showcasing its superior adaptability to real-time traffic conditions at multiple consecutive intersections. This adaptability optimizes traffic flow and contributes to a reduction in environmental impact. This discovery emphasizes the significance of implementing dynamic traffic management solutions tailored to the specific dynamics of urban environments. Based on these findings, the study advocates for the adoption of actuated traffic management systems in cities struggling with similar traffic challenges, highlighting their potential to bolster urban mobility and sustainability. The research also advocates for further exploration into the scalability of these systems and their integration into broader smart city frameworks. By contributing to the ongoing discourse on urban traffic management, this study provides valuable insights that can inform policy-making and the deployment of intelligent traffic solutions.

articleTitle: Wearable sensors for cardiorespiratory monitoring: solutions and applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Workshop on Quantum & Biomedical Applications, Technologies, and Sensors (Q-BATS)
abstract: This work aims at proposing a literature overview of the most popular wearable devices that exploit a single measurement technique for respiratory rate (RR) and heart rate (HR) monitoring. These sensing solutions are grouped into systems based on strain, vibration, and biopotential sensing. For each group, background and working principle are detailed with information on the main solutions proposed in terms of design and composition materials. Moreover, the study covers the description of the key signal processing techniques employed to extract RR and HR from raw data recorded by the wearable devices. Finally, a description of the main application scenarios, with particular emphasis on clinical, sports, and occupational settings, and a brief overview of system performance in these contexts are provided. Challenges and future prospects are also discussed, offering a comprehensive view of these systems and potential advancements for enhancing their real-world applicability.

articleTitle: Energy harvesting techniques and circuits for maritime applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Workshop on Quantum & Biomedical Applications, Technologies, and Sensors (Q-BATS)
abstract: This work presents the basic concepts of energy harvesting (EH) techniques and circuits, with reference to maritime applications. The main EH sources and related sensors are recalled as well as the DC-DC conversion circuits. Multi-input energy sources, piezoelectric and thermoelectric, have been considered. Algorithms for maximum power point tracking are also cited as well as energy storage options. Matlab-Simulink models are finally described.

articleTitle: Proof of Concept for Guarantees of Origin
publicationTitle: 2024 International Workshop on Quantum & Biomedical Applications, Technologies, and Sensors (Q-BATS)
abstract: In the context of the European Green Deal, announced in December 2019, the European Union has committed significant resources to promote clean and sustainable energy, with the aim of achieving climate neutrality by 2050. In line with these initiatives, this article explores the issues related to the transparency and security of Guarantees of Origin (GO) in the energy sector. It examines how the integration of blockchain technology by the Energy Services Manager (GSE) can address these issues, thus contributing to the goals of the European Green Deal and the transition towards a more sustainable and transparent energy economy.

articleTitle: Developing an electronic device for the acquisition and processing of ECG signals: a Soft Computing approach
publicationTitle: 2024 International Workshop on Quantum & Biomedical Applications, Technologies, and Sensors (Q-BATS)
abstract: Future healthcare needs accurate results when using specific sensors that produce exponentially attenuated signals. Due to their applicability in various applications, these sensors are of great interest, including those of a biomedical nature. This paper illustrates a biomedical device capable of analysing and capturing exponentially amortised signals in the biomedical field. The device is intended to capture and study ECG signals and consists of an analogue-digital converter (ADC), a programable connection transistor (PUT), two Thomas Tow square cells, a PGA (programable gain amplifier), and a bi-stable multivibrator with a 555 timer. The device, connected to 10 electrodes, integrates an on-board analysis system to assess the qualitative trend of the signal. ECG signal analysis is performed using a soft computing approach based on the Hybrid ResNet algorithm merged with LSTM (HRL). Finally, as in the results, the soft computing analysis of the implemented system produced encouraging results for both performance and information quality.

articleTitle: Emerging Dynamics in the Electricity Markets: Net Zero Transition through Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Workshop on Quantum & Biomedical Applications, Technologies, and Sensors (Q-BATS)
abstract: This paper provides an overview of the power value chain, from production to trading in European markets highlighting the need for thorough statistical analysis, the use of advanced mathematical-financial modelling, and the application of machine learning to improve the forecasting and management of energy production from renewable sources.Machine learning techniques are employed to develop short- and medium-term forecast models, enhancing the speed and accuracy of predictions and, consequently, the management of renewable energy production. Additionally, these models support the planning of sales and energy storage strategies, contributing to the stability of the electrical grid and hence maximizing profits.In a forthcoming paper, we will focus on enhancing these models and exploring further applications of AI techniques to improve the efficiency and reliability of the energy system by enriching the scientific discussions with diagrams and simulations.
